title: Preparing Protein Producing Synthetic Cells using Cell Free Bacterial Extracts, Liposomes and Emulsion Transfer
protocol: Streak plate E. coli BL21(DE3) bacteria transformed with pAR1219 plasmid on LB-agar with 50 µg/mL ampicillin.
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL of LB-media supplemented with 50 µg/mL ampicillin in a 100 mL flask.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C and 250 rpm using a floor incubator shaker.
Inoculate each 5 mL starter separately into 500 mL of TB media supplemented with 50 µg/mL ampicillin in 2 L flasks with baffles.
Grow the cultures at 37 °C and 250 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.8-1.
Monitor periodically using a spectrophotometer.
Add 2-3 mL of 100 mM IPTG stock to each culture to reach 0.4 - 0.6 mM for induction.
Continue growing the cultures at 37 °C and 250 rpm until OD600≈4.
Transfer solution from each flask into two 250 mL sterilized centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge each tube at 7,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend each pellet in 250 mL of cold (4°C) S30 lysate buffer.
Centrifuge at 7,000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend all pellets together in 15 mL of cold S30 lysate buffer.
Filter the suspension using a gauze pad.
Homogenize the suspension at a working pressure of 15,000 psi with an air pressure of 4 bar (two passes).
Add 100 μL of 0.1 M DTT per 10 mL of homogenized suspension.
Centrifuge the suspension at 24,700 x g for 30 min at 4°C.
Divide the supernatant into 200 μL aliquots in precooled 1.5 mL vials.
Snap freeze the aliquots with liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen aliquots at -80°C for further use.
Dissolve POPC in chloroform to a final concentration of 100 mg/mL.
Vortex the POPC solution separately.
Dissolve cholesterol in chloroform to a final concentration of 100 mg/mL.
Vortex the cholesterol solution separately.
Add 50 µL of POPC in chloroform to a 2 mL glass vial.
Add 50 µL of cholesterol in chloroform to the same vial.
Add 500 µL of mineral oil to the vial.
Vortex the combined components.
Heat the mixture for about 1 hour at 80 °C in a chemical hood to evaporate the chloroform.
Monitor the solution volume to ensure complete evaporation has occurred.
Store the lipid-in-oil solution at room temperature for up to two weeks.
Dissolve glucose in DNase/RNase-free H2O to a final concentration of 200 mM.
Prepare 100 μL of inner solution according to the amounts and concentrations listed in Table 2.
Add UPW to complete the required volume for the inner solution.
Store the mixture at 4°C for a few hours if necessary.
Prepare 1.6 mL of outer solution for each 100 µL of inner solution as per the protocol.
Mix glucose solution with reagents 1-14 according to Table 2 instructions to prepare the final synthetic cell volume of 100 µL.
Incubate at room temperature for 20 min after adding lipids in oil solution on top of 12 mL outer solution in a 15 mL tube.
Mix the inner solution ingredients on crushed ice to a final volume of 100 μL.
Add 100 μL of the inner solution to the second 2 mL glass vial containing 500 μL of lipids in oil solution.
Pipette up and down vigorously for 1 minute.
Vortex the mixture for another minute on level five.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes on crushed ice.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 100 x g and 4 °C.
Centrifuge again for 10 min at 400 x g and 4 °C.
Observe a pellet at the bottom of the tube after centrifugation.
Extract the pellet using a trimmed pipette tip loaded with approximately 400 μL of outer solution.
Release the outer solution while passing through the oil phase to collect only the pellet in the aqueous phase.
Wipe the tip after extracting the pellet to avoid transferring oil remains.
Transfer the pellet to a clean 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 1,000 x g and 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the pellet in 100 µL of feeding solution (1:1 ratio of inner:feeding solutions).
Incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C without shaking.
Prepare a complete inner solution (with DNA & S30-T7 lysate) for activity confirmation.
Immediately incubate the reaction using a floor incubator shaker at 250 rpm or a thermomixer at 1200 rpm, at a constant temperature of 37 °C for 2 h.
Prepare negative control group protocol with inner solution without DNA.
Prepare positive control group protocol with inner solution containing a T7 plasmid encoding for a reporter gene.
